msca-pf-ef.summary: No call is open today (2026-11-04). The 2026 call (HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01) ran from 9 April to 9 September 2026, with results due around February 2027. The next call, HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01-01, is listed as forthcoming on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and the MSCA site: planned opening 7 April 2027, deadline 8 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. Some sources still mark these dates as provisional, so check the portal before relying on them. European Fellowships last 12–24 months at a host in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. They pay the researcher living, mobility and, where applicable, family allowances, and pay the host research, training, networking, management and indirect costs. The host PI/organisation writes the proposal with the fellow, submits it, and if funded employs and supervises the fellow. Carlos appears eligible for the 2027 call. His PhD (expected March 2027) would be awarded before the September 2027 deadline, he is well within the 8-year limit, and he has lived only in Spain. That means any host outside Spain (for example Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Sweden or Switzerland) meets the mobility rule. A Spanish host would not. Because his 2025 Copenhagen visit was short, Denmark should still be fine as a host. As an EU national he could also apply for a Global Fellowship to the US or Canada, which adds a mandatory 12-month return phase in Europe. Host institutions often set internal deadlines between April and July, so he should contact host PIs early in 2027.
msca-pf-ef.eligibility: Any nationality (European Fellowships). You need a PhD by the call deadline; a defended thesis counts even before the degree is formally awarded. You can have at most 8 years of research experience after the PhD; career breaks, work outside research, parental leave and long sick leave are not counted. Mobility rule: in the 36 months before the deadline, you must not have lived or had your main activity (work, studies) in the host country for more than 12 months. From 2026, a proposal that scored below 80% the year before cannot be resubmitted with the same host and researcher. Global Fellowships are open only to EU nationals or long-term residents.
msca-pf-ef.duration: 12–24 months (European Fellowships). Global Fellowships are 24–36 months: 12–24 months outside Europe plus a mandatory 12-month return phase. An optional non-academic placement of up to 6 months is possible at the end.
msca-pf-ef.funding: Unit-cost funding. The researcher receives a living allowance (adjusted by the host country's correction coefficient), a mobility allowance, and, where applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances; employer social security costs are included. The host receives research, training and networking costs plus management and indirect costs. The 2027 indicative budget is about €330M for European Fellowships and €58M for Global Fellowships. I couldn't confirm the exact monthly rates from official pages in this search; they are in the MSCA Work Programme 2026–2027.

humboldt-rf.summary: The current call is closed because it reached the cap of 800 applications. The next call opens on 15 November 2026 and feeds the July 2027 selection meeting. There is no fixed deadline: since 2026 each call closes as soon as 800 applications come in, so applicants should submit on or right after opening day. A draft can be saved in the portal now. Calls open three times a year, on 15 March, 15 July and 15 November. Carlos appears eligible. He is a Spanish national who has not lived in Germany, so the 90-days-in-the-last-18-months rule should not affect him as long as his Copenhagen visit and other stays were outside Germany. His expected PhD date (March 2027) falls before the July 2027 selection meeting, which the rules allow if he submits a written summary of his thesis findings. Strong host options include Brouwer and von Oppen (FU Berlin) and Hassler (RWTH Aachen). His doctoral supervisor cannot be the host.
humboldt-rf.eligibility: Non-German researchers with a doctorate completed within the last 4 years, or completed before the selection meeting (with a written summary of findings). Mothers get up to 2 extra years per child, capped at 6 years. Applicants must not have spent more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying, nor been funded from German sources or done doctoral work in Germany during that time. German nationals and people educated in Germany are eligible only after more than 10 years abroad (or more than 5 years with strong ties to their country of residence). Former Humboldt fellows or award winners cannot apply. Applications are submitted directly by the researcher, together with a mentoring agreement from the host.
humboldt-rf.duration: 6–24 months for postdocs, which can be split into up to 3 stays within 3 years. Each stay lasts at least 6 months, or two 3-month blocks. An optional 2–4-month German language course before the stay does not count toward this.
humboldt-rf.funding: €3,000 per month for postdocs, plus a family allowance, a subsidy for private health insurance and a travel allowance. The host institute receives €800 per month for natural sciences. Expected success rate is 20–25%.

dfg-walter-benjamin.summary: There are no call windows. The DFG Walter Benjamin Programme takes proposals at any time through the elan portal, and a decision takes about 6 months on average. It funds early-career postdocs to carry out their own project, usually for up to two years. In Germany you hold a postdoc position at the host, normally paid at 100%, plus €250 a month for project, travel and publication costs. Abroad you get a fellowship instead (basic amount plus allowances). Carlos appears eligible for the German position, for example with Brouwer or von Oppen at FU Berlin or Hassler at RWTH Aachen: that track has no nationality or prior-Germany-work rules, and he would be changing institution from ICMM-CSIC. He can submit once his dissertation has been handed in (expected around early 2027, with proof of submission and a supervisor statement), but funding only starts after the doctorate is completed. That makes a start around late 2027 realistic. He is not eligible for the abroad fellowship (for example a stay in Copenhagen), because he has not been integrated into the German research system.
dfg-walter-benjamin.eligibility: For postdocs in the early phase after the doctorate (EU 'recognised researcher', R2). DFG sets no fixed number of years since the PhD, and parental leave is taken into account. You can submit once the dissertation has been handed in, but funding starts only after the doctorate is completed. You must generally change institution (not the PhD institution or current one, except with special justification). You must not have worked more than one year at the chosen host when you submit. German position: no nationality or prior-Germany restrictions. Abroad fellowship: you need to have worked at least 3 continuous years in Germany just before the proposal, or have done most of your schooling and higher education in Germany with no more than 3 years abroad for research since the PhD. Carlos does not meet these. The host cannot be for-profit and must allow open publication.
dfg-walter-benjamin.duration: As a rule up to 24 months. The German position and the abroad fellowship modules can be combined. In France, fellowships are limited to 12 months unless you move to a second French institution.
dfg-walter-benjamin.funding: German position: a postdoc post ('postdoctoral researcher and comparable'), usually at 100%, plus €250 a month for direct project, travel and publication costs. The exact pay scale is not stated. Non-university institutes (Max Planck, Helmholtz, Fraunhofer) must guarantee 45% of the position's funding. Abroad fellowship: a monthly basic amount plus foreign, cost-of-living and travel allowances and benefits for children, paid directly to the fellow.

la-caixa-junior-leader-incoming.summary: The Junior Leader Incoming 2027 call opened on 1 July 2026 and closed on 23 September 2026 at 14:00 Spanish time. The foundation's Spanish page now marks it 'Cerrada' (closed). Shortlisting is due 12 January 2027, interviews 16–17 February 2027 and results 10 March 2027. Fellows start between 1 May and 31 December 2027. Dates for the next call (Incoming 2028) have not been announced. Based on past cycles, it should open around July 2027 and close in late September or early October 2027. The fellowship lasts up to 3 years and is worth up to €320,100 in total. That covers employment costs of up to €64,000 a year (minimum gross salary €47,000 a year) and €38,500 a year for research costs, plus family and mobility allowances. Carlos is NOT currently eligible, for two reasons. (1) His PhD is expected in March 2027, but the PhD must be at least 2 years old at the deadline, so the earliest call he could apply to is the one with a deadline around September 2029. (2) He has lived in Spain all his life, so he fails the Incoming mobility rule for Spanish hosts: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in Spain in the 3 years before the deadline. He could become eligible for a Spanish host, such as a Severo Ochoa or María de Maeztu centre, after about 2 or more years of postdoc work abroad. Alternatively, he could apply to a host in Portugal, because the mobility rule there is about time spent in Portugal, which he would meet once the PhD-age rule is satisfied. The sister 'Retaining' modality requires at least 12 months in Spain plus at least 6 months of research abroad, and has the same rule that the PhD must be 2–7 years old.
la-caixa-junior-leader-incoming.eligibility: Any nationality. PhD obtained 2–7 years before the call deadline; for the 2027 call that meant between 23 September 2019 and 23 September 2024, with extensions in specific cases. Incoming mobility rule: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in Spain in the 3 years before the deadline if the host is in Spain; the same rule applies to Portugal for Portuguese hosts. The project must be in a STEM field at an eligible accredited university or research centre in Spain or Portugal.
la-caixa-junior-leader-incoming.funding: Up to €320,100 in total (2027 call). Employment costs up to €64,000 a year, with a minimum gross salary of €47,000 a year. Research costs of €38,500 a year, covering consumables, equipment, travel, conferences and staff. Family allowance of €1,200 a year per dependent child. Mobility allowance of €5,400 for researchers who relocate. These figures come from the 2027 call (20 fellowships per modality).

la-caixa-junior-leader-retaining.summary: The Retaining call that opened in 2026 (called the 'Retaining Call 2027') closed on 2026-09-23 at 14:00 Peninsular Spain time. Pre-selection results and interview invitations are due on 2027-01-12, interviews on 2027-02-24/25 and final results on 2027-03-10. The next Retaining call has not been announced. Based on past cycles it should open around July 2027 and close in late September 2027; these dates are estimates. Carlos is NOT eligible yet: the PhD must have been awarded 2–7 years before the closing date, and his defence is expected in March 2027. That gives him only about 6 months by a September 2027 deadline. The first call he can enter is the one closing around September 2029, or later. To use the Retaining route he must also have lived or worked in Spain for more than 12 months of the 3 years before that deadline. If he does a postdoc abroad from 2027 to 2029 he will probably fail that rule, and the Incoming call (for people who spent less than 12 months in Spain in the last 3 years, hosted at Severo Ochoa or María de Maeztu centres) would fit him instead. He also needs at least 6 months of research stays outside Spain. His 2025 Copenhagen visit counts only if it, plus any other stays abroad, adds up to 6 months.
la-caixa-junior-leader-retaining.eligibility: Any nationality. PhD awarded 2–7 years before the call's closing date, counted from the thesis defence; extended limits apply for career interruptions. For a Spanish host: lived in Spain, or worked/studied there as the main activity, for more than 12 months in the 3 years before the deadline (the same rule applies to Portugal for Portuguese hosts). At least 6 months of research stays abroad (outside the host country) during the PhD or postdoc, continuous or cumulative, before the closing date. STEM fields, including physics.
la-caixa-junior-leader-retaining.funding: Up to €320,100 in total per fellowship over 3 years, covering salary plus research costs. The sources found do not give the exact split between salary and research budget.
